newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 26.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 26.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and
Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
FRANKFURT - Rising costs coupled with lower advertising budgets
have meant German firms are demanding more effective
advertising, an industry survey finds. The GWA advertisers
federation said 130 out of 160 agencies that took part in the
survey said the demonstrable effectiveness of an advertising
campaign was becoming more important for their clients. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - More German companies are using advertising to
attract customers seeking to do business by telephone, German
direct marketing federation DDV says. Client service telephone
numbers are thus becoming an increasingly prominent part of an
advert. Telemarketing, teleshopping and telebanking are moreover
perceived as booming at the moment, with DDV estimating that in
1996 some 3.7 billion marks ($2.1 billion) was spent on
telemarketing campaigns. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Some 54 agencies with 99 campaigns are competing for
this year's Effie awards for effective and creative advertising.
Winners are to be announced on August 28 with a prize ceremony
to be held in Berlin on October 31. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
BONN - Deutsche Telekom AG denies a newspaper report that it
plans a large increase in cable rental charges. While not ruling
out an increase, a Telekom spokesman says a report in the Die
Welt newspaper that it planned to increase cable charges per
household from 20 marks a month to 100 marks was wide off the
mark. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - TV shopping channel Home Order Television (H.O.T)
will be available as part of the DF1 subscription package June
21. (Horizont)
DARMSTADT - Software firm DB-Soft AG Software says its chief
executive Burkhard Stiller had applied to start bankruptcy
proceedings for the firm, amid chronic cashflow problems and
following a vote by shareholders last Saturday against a
proposal to sell the company. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
INGOLSTADT - Carmaker Audi AG, a unit of Volkswagen, expects
record sales and earnings in 1997, thanks in part to strong
demand for its new A6 saloon. 1997 sales are due to top 20
billion marks and pre-tax profit is seen exceeding the 1996
level of 862 million marks. Audi also expects to sell more than
500,000 vehicles around the world during the year and expected
first-half sales to rise 16 percent to 10.8 billion marks.
(Reuter)
HAMBURG - Brewery group Holsten is seeing yet another fall in
beer production during the current year. In the first four
months, volumes shrunk 2.1 percent and domestic beer sales
slipped 3.8 percent, the company says. Growth is coming from
exports, with Asia and Latin America both strong. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Daimler-Benz AG says it would quit its six-year
stake in computer systems firm Cap Gemini SA, killing
speculation it planned a takeover of the French company. Daimler
is to pull out of Gap Gemini because of differing strategic
focuses and because a U.S. Bank Holding Company Act hindered Cap
Gemini's business there. Daimler currently holds 24.4 percent in
Cap Gemini. (Reuter)
BONN - German cosmetics and drugstore chain Douglas Holding
reports group sales in the first five months of this year up 5.7
percent to 1.57 billion marks, while earnings were just down on
last year. Chief executive Joern Kreke tells Douglas's annual
shareholders meeting the company will devote all its efforts
this year to break a run of stagnant results and beat its
previous record profit of 227 million marks in 1993.
PEOPLE NEWS:
HAMBURG - Former Kaufhof-chief Jens Odewald has been appointed
head of the supervisory board of coffee-roaster Tchibo Holding,
replacing Ronaldo Schmitz. (Reuter)
Frankfurt - Thorsten Moe, head of press for Japanese video game
firm Sega's German office, is now also taking over marketing
responsibilities from Andreas von Gliszcynski. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Andreas von Maltzan, 32, is to lead the newly-formed
sales and marketing department of tm3, the commercial TV channel
aimed at women. (Kress)
